summary: Toru Haneda was a scholar of Central Asian studies, sinology, and history and archaeology. He studied at the Third Higher School, the University of Tokyo, and Kyoto University, where he served as professor, dean of letters, and director.

Toru Kumeji works in Buddhist studies and computational humanities. He has held positions at the Center for Open Humanities Data and the Humanities Information Studies Institute, where he was attested as senior researcher in 2015.

Toru Sagara was a scholar of philosophy and Japanology who studied under Tetsuro Watsuji at the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Ibaraki University (~1950–1966), the University of Tokyo (~1966–1982), and Kyoritsu Women's University (~1982–1993).

Toru Takahashi was a scholar of sinology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. After studying at the University of Tokyo, he held posts including professor at Keijo Imperial University (1926–1940), Fukuoka University (1949), and Tenri University (1950–1964).

Toru Tomabechi is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at Kyoto University and the University of Lausanne, and later held positions at the Humanities Information Studies Institute and the Center for Open Humanities Data.
Toshiaki Yamada is a scholar of sinology and religious studies. He studied at Toyo University from approximately 1966 to 1976 and served on the faculty there from around 1981 to 2017.

Toshifumi Goto is a scholar of Indology and linguistics who earned his PhD at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg in 1982 under Karl Hoffmann. He served as professor at Osaka University and Tohoku University.
Toshihide Unebe is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Issai Funahashi. He served as a professor at Doho University, attested in 1991.

Toshihiko Izutsu was a scholar of philosophy, linguistics, and religious studies. After graduating from Keio University, he served as a professor there (1954–1981), at McGill University (1969–1975), and at the Iranian Institute of Philosophy (1975–1979).

Toshihiko Kimura is an Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tohoku University. He taught at Tohoku University, served as associate professor at Tokai Gakuin University, and is professor emeritus at Shitennoji University.
Toshihiro Wada is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied under Vashishtha Narayan Jha in 1981. He served as a professor at Nagoya University from approximately 1990 to 2020.

Toshiichi Endo is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Kelaniya and completed a doctorate at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies supervised by Mahinda Palihawadana and W. S. Karunatillake.

Toshikazu Watanabe is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He worked as a researcher at the Austrian Academy of Sciences, attested from 2011 to 2015, and became a professor at Kokugakuin University in 2018.

Toshiki Osada is a linguist and Indologist who studied at Hokkaido University. He held positions at Kyoto University of the Arts (~1993–2003) and served as a professor and project leader at the Research Institute for Humanity and Nature (~2003–2019).

Toshinori Ochiai is a Buddhist studies, sinology, and Japanology scholar. He has served at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies, Kacho Junior College, the Institute for the Study of Ancient Manuscript Buddhist Canons, and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.
Toshio Ando was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University from approximately 1930 to 1933. He held academic posts at Doho University and Otani University (~1944–1973).

Toshio Horiuchi is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy who earned his PhD from the University of Tokyo in 2009. He held posts at Toyo University (~2011–2017) and Zhejiang University (~2017).

Toshio Nagahiro was an archaeologist, sinologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University. He served at Kyoto University's Institute for Research in Humanities, became a university professor there (~1957–1969), and later was president of Kyoto Tachibana University.

Toshio Sako is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Jikido Takasaki and Yasunori Ejima, and at Columbia University with doctoral supervisor Alex Wayman.

Toshio Yamazaki was a scholar of Indology and history and archaeology. He held posts at Tokyo Institute of Technology, Hannan University, and Chuo University, and was named professor emeritus at the University of Tokyo.
